question: Which official Linux companion architecture and ownership boundary should OpenClaw endorse now that Windows Hub exists but Linux remains planned?
rationale: The remaining work is a multi-surface product and security decision involving desktop runtime choice, remote-gateway authentication, node capabilities, packaging, updates, and parity scope; source inspection cannot safely select a permanent direction without owner intent.

options.title: Keep umbrella; choose Linux direction
options.body: Retain this issue as the canonical program tracker, recognize Windows Hub as the current Windows path, and select one Linux implementation direction before accepting further broad work.

options.title: Split platform trackers
options.body: Close the Windows portion as addressed by Windows Hub and create or designate a separate owner-backed Linux companion tracker with explicit architecture and security criteria.

options.title: Defer official Linux app
options.body: Keep Linux gateway support terminal-first and direct community companion work to external projects until a maintainer sponsors an official desktop direction.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella; choose Linux direction
recommendation.body: Retain this issue as the canonical program tracker, recognize Windows Hub as the current Windows path, and select one Linux implementation direction before accepting further broad work.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue originator supplied the stated product vision, prioritized security and core work, and is the strongest visible source of platform-direction intent in the discussion.
